prayerExcerpt.en-US: May we experience their loving intercession for us in your presence.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Concedei-nos experimentar sua intercessão em nosso favor.

meta.face: Two clearly different men. Nereus (left, the elder): a man of about forty-five with a BLOCKY, FLAT-TOPPED head and a strong, wide face — a heavy, straight brow ridge, deep-set steady dark eyes, a thick, strong nose with a slight bend at the bridge, broad cheekbones and a wide, square jaw with a wide, firm mouth; short, soldier-cropped black hair greying at the temples and a close, dark stubble beard; a sober, resolute look. Achilleus (right, the younger): a slender man of about twenty-eight, clean-shaven, with a LONG face and HIGH, ROUNDED cheekbones over a squared-off chin — a thin, straight nose, large bright light-brown eyes under fine, arched brows, a small, well-cut mouth; short, light-brown hair in tight curls; his gaze lifted a little, hopeful.
meta.basis: Pope Damasus's epitaph at their tomb says they were soldiers who, suddenly converted, threw away their shields, decorations and bloody weapons and died confessing Christ; the carved pillar of their ciborium in the Domitilla basilica shows Achilleus's execution. No likeness survives; the elder, blocky Nereus and the younger, long-faced Achilleus are our choice, echoing Rubens's pairing of an older and a younger man.
